In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel method for the preparation of 3-substituted indoles and indole-3-acetic acids.
the development and applications of the theory of the chemical shift and the nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy.
the effects of the out-of- plane vibrations on the hfsc of a HFSC of the bicyclo [2.1. 1] hexan-5- yl radical.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the hfsc of H6endo is sensitive to the out-of-plane motion of the C5-H5 bond and the sensitivity of the hfsc to the out-of plane motion of the bond is larger than the sensitivity of the isotropic hyperfine coupling constant of the H6 atom to the out-of- plane motion of the C4–H4 bond.
the increase in the hfsc of the H6endo radical is due to the decrease in the out-of-plane vibrational amplitude of the C5-H6 bond.

the hfsc of the bicyclo-[2.1.2]heptan-6-yl radical is increased from 27.6 G to 28 G, and that of the bicyclo[-2.1.0]pentyl radical is increased by 0.5–2.2 G by the replacement of the C–H bond with a C–D bond.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hfsc’s for the C–H bonds of the radicals are sensitive to the out-of-plane vibration of the C–H bond, and this is the first example for a long-range isotope effect on the hfsc’s of radicals.
the hfscs of H5 and H6 are affected by the out-of-plane and in-plane vibrations of the C5-C5 bond, respectively, and that the in-plane vibration of the C6-C6 bond affects the hfscs only of H6endo.

the hfscs of the H6endo and H6exo protons of the bicyclo-[2.1. 1]hexyl radical, which are the most important parameters for the determination of its geometry, have been determined by ESR spectroscopy and that the geometry of this radical has been determined by the combination of ESR and ab initio calculations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a long-range isotope effect can be observed for the hfscs of the bicyclohexanyl and bicyclopentanyl radicals.
, in the presence of a long-range isotopic effect, the out-of-plane vibration of a C–H bond is a key factor for determining the hfsc of a hydrogen atom attached to that carbon.
the long-range effect of an isotopically labeled atom can be detected in the hfsc of the H6endo proton, and the effect is due to the change in the out-of-plane motion of the C5-H5 bond.
